To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) factorized models are more effective than non-factorized models, b) the factorization into multiword expressions and supersenses is more effective than factorization into other label types, c) the 2-CRF model is more effective than the CRF model, and d) the 2-PCFG model is not more effective than the PCFG model.

1) a first-order CRF model with a factorization of labels into multiword expressions and supersenses performs better than a second-order CRF model, and that 2) adding a second-order model to the first-order model improves performance.

(i) the use of a factorization of labels into two parts, MWEs and supersenses, improves the accuracy of both parts; (ii) the use of second-order features improves accuracy; and (iii) the use of the second-order CRF model is not as beneficial for MWE detection as it is for supersense detection.
